topics.titleTr: Tablolar İçin ChatGPT mi Gemini mi: Gerçek Test

topics.angle: comparison + which to trust for data analysis and formulas
topics.brief: Data-led hands-on comparison of ChatGPT vs Gemini for spreadsheet work. Sections: ChatGPT's Code Interpreter for uploads, charts and Python-driven analysis; Gemini's native Sheets/Workspace integration and formula generation; accuracy on messy data, pivots and multi-step transforms; when each wins (workbook Q&A vs in-Google workflow); privacy of uploaded files; verification habits. Verify: current Code Interpreter capabilities and Gemini-in-Sheets features; both models' file-handling limits. Sources: itGenius and datastudios spreadsheet comparisons; provider docs. No corpus post covers spreadsheets. End with a 'pick by workflow' recommendation and a prompt cheat-sheet.

topics.titleEn: Build a Second Brain With AI in 2026
topics.angle: how-to + capture, organize and retrieve knowledge that compounds
topics.brief: Field-notes how-to on building an AI-powered second brain. Sections: the capture-organize-distill-retrieve loop (PARA/CODE basics); tool choices by priority (Notion for all-in-one, Obsidian for private/local, Mem/Tana for auto-organization, NotebookLM for cited research); letting AI tag, summarize and surface without becoming a junk drawer; keeping notes you actually own and can export; retrieval that beats search. Verify: current AI features and pricing of the named tools and export/portability. Sources: taskade and buildin.ai 2026 second-brain roundups. Distinct from prompt-library and organize-your-AI-chats posts. End with a starter workflow and tool-by-need table.

topics.titleTr: AI Çalışma Araçları: NotebookLM, ChatGPT, Gemini

topics.angle: comparison + which fits notes, revision and exam prep
topics.brief: Question-driven comparison of AI study tools for students in 2026. Sections: NotebookLM's cited notes from your own sources; ChatGPT's new interactive quizzes and study/Think modes; Gemini's Classroom study tools (flashcards, practice quizzes, study guides, guided prompts); which fits reading vs active recall vs group study; cost and student offers; avoiding the 'AI does the thinking' trap. Verify: the Aug 2026 ChatGPT interactive-quiz and Gemini-in-Classroom study features and student free-tier offers. Sources: OpenAI ChatGPT release notes; blog.google Classroom/Gemini student posts. Distinct from the single-tool NotebookLM study post. End with a per-goal recommendation.

End with a task-to-model routing table.

Sources: tool docs and release notes; reproducible benchmark posts. Distinct from the biome-vs-oxlint (linters) and TypeScript-7 (compiler) posts. End with a chooser by framework and project size.

Verify: the core chaos-engineering principles and typical starter experiments; blast-radius safety practices. Sources: Principles of Chaos Engineering; tool docs (Litmus, AWS FIS). Distinct from incident-response-for-small-teams and backups/DR posts. End with a first-GameDay checklist and a hypothesis template.
